subject: physics_2
question_text: The Lyman series of hydrogen spectrum lies in the ultraviolet region. Why?

mark_split.label: The wavelengths 912 Å to 1216 Å are ultraviolet

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. The book prints "lyman" in lower case; the name is capitalised here and the angstrom is written Å rather than the book's "A°". Physics hand-checked with 1/λ = R(1/n₁² − 1/n₂²), R = 1.097 × 10⁷ m⁻¹: n₂ = 2 → n₁ = 1 gives λ = 1216 Å (the longest line) and n₂ = ∞ → n₁ = 1 gives λ = 912 Å (the series limit). Both are shorter than 4000 Å, the short-wavelength end of the visible band, so the whole series is ultraviolet.

recall_prompt: Say which level the Lyman transitions end on, and the two wavelengths that fix the series in the ultraviolet.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Transitions end on n₁ = 1
lines: The Lyman series is emitted when the electron
moves from an outer orbit to the first orbit
(n₁ = 1). This is the largest energy drop in
hydrogen, so the photon energy is the largest
steps.margin_note: First mark. Name the final level n₁ = 1 and link big energy to short wavelength.
steps.why: λ = hc/ΔE. The n = 1 level lies far below all the others, so every Lyman transition releases a large ΔE and therefore a short wavelength.
common_mistakes: Saying the transitions end on n = 2. That is the Balmer series.
Saying a large energy gives a long wavelength. λ is inversely proportional to ΔE.

recall.must_convey: That Lyman transitions end on n₁ = 1, the largest energy drop, so the wavelength is shortest.
accept: electron comes to the first orbit
largest energy difference so shortest wavelength

steps.memory_tip: Lowest final level, biggest drop, shortest wavelength.

steps.label: The wavelength range
lines: The shortest and longest wavelengths of the
Lyman series are 912 Å and 1216 Å.
The visible band starts near 4000 Å, so both
of these lie well below it.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Quote both limits and compare with 4000 Å.
steps.why: The two limits bracket the whole series: 1216 Å from n₂ = 2 and 912 Å from n₂ = ∞. Every line between them is shorter than 4000 Å, which is what makes the series ultraviolet.
common_mistakes: Calling this the visible region. The visible band is 4000 Å to 7000 Å.
Quoting only one wavelength. Both limits show the whole series is ultraviolet.

recall.must_convey: That the series runs from 912 Å to 1216 Å, below the visible band, so it is ultraviolet.
accept: nine one two angstrom to one two one six angstrom
reject: electron comes to the first orbit

steps.memory_tip: 912 and 1216 — both are far short of the 4000 Å where visible light begins.

insider_note: The reason earns the first mark and the two numbers earn the second — 912 Å and 1216 Å are the ones to quote.
